title: Aotearoa Animals
subject: Science
source: Native and introduced animals of New Zealand

questions.q: Which New Zealand bird is the heaviest parrot in the world and cannot fly?
questions.explanation: The kākāpō is a big, flightless, night-time parrot. It is the heaviest parrot in the world.

questions.q: Which cheeky parrot lives in the mountains of the South Island?
questions.explanation: Kea are alpine parrots, famous for being curious and cheeky.

questions.q: True or false: kiwi are nocturnal, which means they are mostly active at night.
questions.explanation: Kiwi sleep in burrows during the day and come out at night to feed.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a wētā?
questions.explanation: Wētā are insects: they have six legs and three body parts.

options: The last living members of an ancient reptile group
questions.explanation: Tuatara look like lizards but belong to their own very old group of reptiles.

questions.q: Which bird has a white tuft of feathers at its throat?
questions.explanation: Tūī have a white tuft of feathers at the throat, often called a poi.

questions.q: What does the pīwakawaka (fantail) mostly eat?
questions.explanation: Fantails flit and fan their tails to catch small flying insects.

options: Giant flightless birds that are now extinct
questions.explanation: Moa were huge flightless birds. They became extinct a few hundred years ago.

questions.q: Which animals are New Zealand's only native land mammals?
questions.explanation: Pekapeka (bats) are our only native land mammals. Possums, stoats and hedgehogs were brought here.

questions.q: Why are stoats a big problem for New Zealand birds?
options: They hunt native birds and eat their eggs
questions.explanation: Stoats are predators. Many of our birds did not evolve to escape them.

questions.q: How does the kererū help native forests?
options: It spreads the seeds of large fruits
questions.explanation: Kererū can swallow big fruits whole and spread their seeds far away, helping new trees grow.

questions.q: What is the yellow-eyed penguin called in te reo Māori?
questions.explanation: The yellow-eyed penguin is the hoiho. The little penguin is the kororā.

questions.q: A living thing that makes its own food from sunlight is called a…
questions.explanation: Plants are producers: they use sunlight to make their own food.

questions.q: A scientist counts the kiwi in a forest every year. What is she doing?
options: Collecting data to look for changes
questions.explanation: Scientists collect data over time so they can notice patterns and changes.

questions.q: True or false: possums are native to New Zealand.
questions.explanation: Possums were brought from Australia in the 1800s and now damage our forests.
